note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. Hypothesis unless sets measured. Stage persona only.

identity.deal: Kill Tony firestarter who turns the everyman situation into a fast, loud, high-energy kill with zero flinch.
identity.premise: A man who treats the stage like a fight he's going to win on volume and commitment alone.
identity.awareness_note: Semi: the energy is the act; the craft is sharpening fast.

philosophy.ontology: The set is a fight and the fight is the point.
philosophy.epistemology: If the room feels it, it's true.
philosophy.axiology: Commitment and energy beat polish; the laugh is a contact sport.
philosophy.causality: One committed escalation can outrun three clean jokes.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can be loud; almost nobody is loud with a point.

dramatic_core.want: the room to feel what he feels before he can name it
dramatic_core.fear: the polite silence — the death of the fight
dramatic_core.need: to be the one they remember from the episode
blind_spots: the firestarter can become a one-volume act

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats the everyman situation as a fight worth having out loud, and escalates until the room concedes.
contradictions: the firestarter with the sharp turn
the loud one with the clean setup
the regular who grew into a force

tells: the laugh that is also a dare

threads: the commit as a comic form
the room as a sparring partner
problem_space: the regular who became a force

essay_seeds.title: Cam Patterson: 'The everyday fight' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: Takes a normal annoyance and treats it as a fight he's going to win on volume and commitment alone. The room is drawn into the fight because the energy is contagious. status_reversal: the person who was losing (to the situation) is now winning (on stage).
outline: what this reveals about the engine

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.
